how-to-price-daycare-tuition.html.text:
← Daycare tuition calculator

How to price daycare tuition without underpricing an empty seat

A per-child tuition rate set by feel, or by matching a nearby center, hides the one number that actually drives a classroom's margin: how full it is. Staffing is scheduled to meet a licensed ratio, not to the exact headcount on any given day, which means an empty seat is rarely a saved cost -- it is almost always lost revenue.

Open the free daycare tuition calculator

What a flat tuition rate does not show

Fixed staffing cost. A room staffed for a 10:1 ratio with two teachers costs the same in wages whether 14 children or 20 are enrolled. Occupancy changes revenue, not cost.

The room and the ratio can each be the limit. A classroom licensed for a 10:1 ratio with two staff has a ratio-based capacity of 20 -- but a smaller room might be licensed for only 15 by square footage. Whichever is smaller is the classroom's real ceiling.

Overhead spread across fewer children. Rent, supplies, and administrative cost allocated to a room do not shrink as enrollment drops, so a half-empty room spreads the same overhead across half as many tuition checks.

Worked example

A 10:1 ratio, two staff at $18/hour, a room licensed for 20, 85% occupancy, 12% payroll burden, $1,500 in monthly overhead, a $900 current tuition rate, and a 10% target margin:

FigureValue
Classroom capacity20 (ratio-bound)
Enrolled at 85% occupancy17
Monthly fixed cost (staff + overhead)$10,236
Break-even tuition per child$602.12
Tuition needed for a 10% margin$669.02
Profit at the current $900 rate$5,064/month (about 33% margin)
Revenue left on 3 empty seats$2,700/month, $32,400/year

The same room at 50% occupancy needs $1,137.33 per child just to clear the same 10% margin on the same fixed cost -- and at the $900 rate actually being charged, it would be losing $1,236 a month rather than earning it. Occupancy moves the required tuition more than almost any realistic price change, because the fixed cost never moves with it.

Common questions

How do I calculate the right tuition for a daycare classroom?

Start from your classroom's own fixed monthly cost — staff wages plus payroll burden, plus overhead allocated to that room — and divide by the number of children you actually expect enrolled, not the room's full licensed capacity. At a 10:1 ratio with two staff, 85% occupancy, $18/hour wages, and $1,500 monthly overhead, that fixed cost is $10,236 a month across 17 enrolled children, a break-even tuition of $602.12 per child before any margin at all.

Why does an empty seat cost so much if nobody is using it?

Because a classroom is staffed to meet its licensed ratio, not to the number of children physically present. Two staff scheduled for a 10:1 room cost the same whether 14 or 20 children show up, so every enrolled seat below capacity is pure lost revenue rather than avoided cost. In the worked example, three empty seats at a $900 tuition rate is $2,700 a month never billed.

Should I raise tuition or fill seats first?

Compare the two against your own fixed cost rather than assuming either one first. Filling the room from 85% to 100% occupancy in the worked example adds 3 more paying families at the current $900 rate without changing the tuition needed to hit margin; raising tuition instead means charging every family more to cover the same fixed cost across fewer children. Occupancy is usually the cheaper lever because it recovers revenue you are already staffed to deliver.

Why the number changes

A classroom's biggest cost -- staff scheduled to meet its licensed ratio -- does not shrink when a seat sits empty. That is what makes occupancy, not the sticker price, the number that actually swings a classroom's margin. This calculator makes the empty-seat cost visible so you can decide whether to hold, market, or reprice a room before the next enrollment cycle.

Search questions answered: how to calculate daycare tuition, how much should daycare cost to break even, and what is a classroom's real capacity given its ratio and room size? See the full pricing guide with a worked example, how this compares to pricing tuition by hand or in a spreadsheet, or how this calculator differs from Procare if you already use childcare management software.

Common questions

Does this tool tell me my state's legal child:staff ratio?

No. Ratios vary by state and by age group and change over time, so this tool never asserts one — you type in the ratio from your own license. It only does the arithmetic once you supply that number, the same way it never checks your room's licensed square-footage capacity for you.

Why is the tuition I need lower than what I actually charge?

Because the required-tuition figure is only large enough to hit your stated target margin, not to match whatever you already charge. At the defaults — a 10:1 ratio, two staff, 85% occupancy, and a 10% target margin — the room only needs $669.02 per child to clear that 10% margin, well under the $900 actually being charged, which is why the current-rate margin comes out to about 33%.

What does one empty seat actually cost me?

Not a lower cost — lost revenue. A classroom is staffed to its licensed ratio, not to the exact number of children present on a given day, so payroll and overhead do not fall when a seat sits empty. At the defaults, three empty seats out of a 20-seat room at $900 tuition is $2,700 a month, $32,400 a year, that never appears on any expense line because it left as revenue that was never billed.

How much does occupancy actually move the tuition I need to charge?

More than price itself, in most rooms, because staffing cost is fixed once a classroom is opened. At the defaults, a full room only needs $568.67 per child to clear a 10% margin; the same room at half-full needs $1,137.33 per child to clear the same margin on the same fixed cost — and at the $900 rate actually being charged, that half-full room is losing $1,236 a month, not just earning less.

Is my enrollment and pricing data uploaded anywhere?

No. Every figure is calculated in your browser and saved only to this browser's local storage so the form remembers your numbers next visit. The Copy shareable link button puts the same numbers in the page's URL fragment, which your browser never sends to a server — nothing is uploaded, and no accounts, analytics vendors, or child or family information is collected.

Running a whole center? The childcare center break-even calculator covers ratios and occupancy.

Running a private school with financial aid? The private school tuition discount calculator turns sticker price and aid groups into net tuition and a discount rate.

Privacy: Everything runs in your browser. Your inputs are never uploaded. The "Reset saved inputs" draft lives only in this browser's local storage, and "Copy shareable link" puts the same numbers in the page's URL fragment instead of a server — nothing about your classroom leaves your device either way. We count only anonymous feature events in local storage, never people, IPs, or content. Clear storage or enable the browser's Do Not Track / Global Privacy Control signal to stop counting.

vs-doing-it-by-hand.html.text:
← Daycare tuition calculator

This calculator vs. pricing tuition by hand or in a spreadsheet

Dividing a room's monthly cost by the number of children enrolled is one line of arithmetic — anyone can do it by hand or in a spreadsheet, and a correctly built spreadsheet gets that division exactly right. What it usually does not do on its own is stay fixed to the room's licensed ratio and overhead as occupancy changes, and recompute what tuition needs to be, and what an empty seat is actually costing you, at every occupancy level rather than just the one you happened to type in today.

That is the narrower job this calculator does. It takes the same inputs a spreadsheet would need — your child:staff ratio, staff scheduled, room capacity, wages, hours, overhead, and target margin — and holds staffing and overhead fixed while it walks occupancy from 50% to 100%, so the tuition needed and the profit at your current rate are visible at every level, not recalculated by hand each time enrollment changes.

QuestionWhere to answer it
What is the break-even tuition per child at today's enrolled count? Either — monthly cost ÷ enrolled children. A spreadsheet gets this exactly right too.
What does a full or half-empty room need to charge to clear a target margin, without rebuilding the sheet? This calculator's occupancy table — six occupancy levels at once, staffing and overhead held fixed. A spreadsheet has to be rebuilt each time you ask this by hand.
What is an empty seat actually costing me right now, in dollars per month and per year? This calculator solves it directly. By hand, it is easy to read an empty seat as a smaller bill rather than the lost revenue it actually is, since staffing does not shrink with enrollment.
Is the room's capacity set by the ratio or by the room's own licensed square footage? Either can check it, but a spreadsheet has to be told to take the smaller of the two — this calculator always does.
I want to try a different wage, overhead figure, or target margin quickly. Either — a well-built spreadsheet updates instantly too, once it is built correctly.
My situation has a wrinkle this calculator doesn't model (a second age group, a sliding tuition scale, a subsidy). A spreadsheet you build yourself — it can represent any rule you can describe.
Is anything I enter uploaded anywhere? No, either way — a local spreadsheet and this calculator both keep your numbers on your own device.

Most directors get different value from each: a spreadsheet for whatever wrinkle their own center has that a general tool will never model, and a calculator like this one for the standard ratio-and-occupancy question answered instantly, without rebuilding a formula every time a wage or an overhead line changes.

It needs no account and no sign-in: it is a static page, the arithmetic runs in your browser, and once it has loaded it keeps working with the connection off.

Common questions

Can't I just divide my monthly cost by the number of children enrolled?

Yes, and that division is exactly right as far as it goes — monthly cost divided by enrolled children is the break-even tuition per child, and a spreadsheet does that multiplication and division exactly as well as this calculator does. Where a hand calculation or a quick spreadsheet formula usually stops is at a single occupancy snapshot: today's enrolled count, today's tuition. It rarely gets rebuilt to show what the same room needs at a different occupancy rate, which is the question that actually decides whether to chase enrollment or raise the rate.

What does a spreadsheet not check that this calculator does?

Whether staffing cost is fixed to the room's ratio rather than to who shows up. A spreadsheet built to divide cost by headcount has no built-in reminder that two staff scheduled for a 10:1 room cost the same whether 14 or 20 children are enrolled -- so an empty seat is easy to model as a smaller bill instead of what it actually is: revenue that was never billed. This calculator holds staffing and overhead fixed and recomputes enrolled children, required tuition, and profit at six occupancy levels at once, so the empty-seat cost is a number on the page rather than a spreadsheet row nobody added.

Is the occupancy table something I could build myself in a spreadsheet?

With the right formulas, yes -- it is the same fixed-cost, ratio-bound-or-room-bound capacity check repeated at each occupancy percentage, with tuition solved backward from a target margin. Setting that up correctly the first time, and re-deriving it correctly every time a wage, an overhead line, or a target margin changes, is exactly the kind of arithmetic that is easy once and easy to get subtly wrong later -- a stale reference to last year's wage or a margin formula that forgot the overhead line does not announce itself the way a typo in a tuition figure does.

Is this calculator affiliated with any spreadsheet software or childcare management platform?

There is nothing to be affiliated with. This page compares against doing the arithmetic by hand or building your own spreadsheet -- a generic method every center director already has access to, not any specific company or product -- so it names no spreadsheet application, childcare management platform, or vendor at all.

vs-procare.html.text:
← Daycare tuition calculator

This calculator vs. Procare

Procare Solutions is a well-known paid childcare management platform, built to run a center's day-to-day operations for a director and staff — enrollment records, attendance and check-in, staff scheduling, and billing families once a tuition rate is already set, sold as an ongoing per-center subscription described on procaresoftware.com. It is the kind of tool a center reaches for once it needs to run enrollment, attendance, and billing across many families and staff at once.

That is a different job from the one this page does. This calculator has no enrollment records, no attendance tracking, and no billing. It exists for the narrower task that comes before any of that: working out what a classroom's tuition needs to be from your own child:staff ratio, staffing cost, hours, overhead, and occupancy, and seeing what an empty seat is actually costing you at your current rate — with nothing to sign up for.

QuestionWhere to answer it
I need to run enrollment records, attendance and check-in, and staff scheduling across my center. Procare or a comparable platform — day-to-day center operations are not something this calculator attempts.
What should this classroom's monthly tuition per child actually be, given its ratio, staffing cost, and occupancy? This calculator — free, instant, private, no account.
How much is an empty seat costing this room right now, at my current tuition rate? This calculator's occupancy table, which holds staffing and overhead fixed as enrollment changes.
I already have a rate. I need to invoice and collect tuition from families every month. Procare or a comparable platform — billing and collection are not this calculator's job.
Do I need to create an account or sign up to use the tool? This calculator: no. Procare is used through a paid subscription account.

Most directors get different value from each: Procare (or a comparable platform) for running enrollment, attendance, and billing as an ongoing subscription, and a private calculator like this one for an instant, no-login check of what a classroom's rate should be before it is entered anywhere for billing. This calculator's own output is a pricing check, not a record of your center's enrollment or billing history.

It needs no account and no sign-in: it is a static page, the arithmetic runs in your browser, and once it has loaded it keeps working with the connection off.

Common questions

Should I use this calculator or a paid platform like Procare?

They answer different questions. Procare Solutions is a paid subscription platform built to run a childcare center's day-to-day operations — enrollment records, attendance and check-in, staff scheduling, and billing families once a tuition rate is already set, described on Procare's own site. This calculator does none of that. It is a free, browser-only page for a narrower job that comes before any of it: working out what a classroom's tuition needs to be from its own ratio, staffing cost, and occupancy, with no account and nothing uploaded. A center running enrollment, attendance, and billing across many families and staff is looking for the wrong tool here; a director who needs to set or check a rate before typing it into a billing system is in the right place.

Does Procare tell me what my tuition rate should be?

Procare bills families at whatever rate a center enters into it; it manages collecting that rate, not deriving it from staffing cost and occupancy. This calculator does the opposite: it takes your ratio, staffing wage, hours, overhead, and occupancy and works out the tuition needed to hit a target margin, and what an empty seat is actually costing you at your current rate — the arithmetic a director does before a rate exists to bill, not the billing itself.

Is this page affiliated with Procare Solutions?

No. This site is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Procare Solutions. Procare is named here only to describe what this calculator is and is not.
